title: Why Dogs Lick You: Penn Vet Says It's Not a Kiss 🐶 (Things Living In Your House)
description:
Why do dogs lick you? A University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine handout says a dog licking a person or another dog is not a "kiss." It is a greeting behavior, but if a dog licks someone repeatedly, he may be anxious about that dog or person. Lip licking is a different signal: Penn Vet lists it as anxiety about a situation or interaction, and AAHA and Texas A&M also list lip licking among nervous or distress signs. A Tufts veterinary behaviorist says an anxious dog may also appear extra friendly and lick a face. Penn Vet also says dogs do not kiss, and they may be frightened by kissing.
